finding: CONTRIBUTING convention text described only the Personio exception to all-or-nothing parsing, omitting the Gem demo-job skip.

finding: A Location that urljoin cannot parse (unclosed IPv6 bracket) raised ValueError out of the redirect handler instead of leaving the redirect as the answer.
note: connections._redirect at ^ no try/except around urljoin

finding: connections had its own URL check that differed from payload.http_url, the adapters' rule.

No test proved a non-200 body is never read (a hung body would time out).

finding: An IPv6 host without a port was read by http.client as host and port because the origin kept port None.

finding: A 200 whose body read fails (timeout) after the server said it closes left the socket open, held by the response, not the connection.

finding: A redirect target with an invalid port was followed as a URL and failed later rather than being the answer; URLs were parsed in several places.
note: connections._redirect at ^ checked scheme/hostname only; port accessed in _exchange

finding: The close test's threads did not overlap, so a reused thread id could mask a lost connection.

finding: A required answer containing a control character (NUL) passed the single-line check but would not come back unchanged from the set-up page's select.
The set-up commands test discarded the check output stream into an inline call, hiding which output it asserted.
A required answer longer than TEXT_LIMIT, or one that pushes the posted form over the page's size limit, was not refused by the tags step or counted by _posted_size.
The UI test's Fields parser kept an options list and picked the chosen value with a nested expression, obscuring what a browser posts when none is selected.
A left-out row could span several lines, since a free-text answer or title with line breaks was printed raw, breaking the digest's structure.
The digest line and require matching each wrote their own warning condition; a default answer with an unverified quote was shown with a warning rule different from the one used to skip it.

finding: fetch_each relied on generator garbage collection to stop a lane pass, so workers could still run after the connections closed when the caller stopped early and a reference outlived the generator.
The README status line named a version that drifts from pyproject.
backup.code_identity's comment claimed every git install reports 0.1.0.
